Answer: A
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 2) shows the mass located anteriorly, overlying the cardiac silhouette and retrosternal space, confirming an anterior mediastinal location. The frontal view (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-defined mass with obtuse angles at the interface with the mediastinum, which is characteristic of an anterior mediastinal lesion such as a substernal goiter (ectopic thyroid).
